semantic_config_snapshot.quarantined_nonsemantic_transport_metada: Branch-head lookup exposed commit metadata beyond the SHA; it was not used as semantic evidence.

scope.tested: One bounded capability audit plus 64-trace finite counterexample model for same owner/name repository delete-recreate/rebind between an identity precheck and mutation. The replacement may either lack or deliberately/importantly reuse the same Git blob/commit history. Response loss and next-invocation retry are toggled independently. Part127 generation/idempotency semantics are held fixed.
assumptions: Same-name replacement is allowed to contain identical file content and/or imported identical Git history, so content-addressed blob/commit SHAs can coincide across the old and replacement repository states.
The stale agent is cooperative and uses only currently Chat-exposed GitHub connector mutation preconditions.
No same-run retry/backoff is used; a response-loss or rate-limit ambiguity is resumed only on a later invocation.
A repository metadata read can expose a repository id/node id, but the tested mutation surfaces do not accept that id as an atomic mutation precondition.
not_tested: GitHub internal guarantees not documented or exposed to the connector
Organization-level policies that forbid repository deletion/recreation
Byzantine mutation of the authority file itself

current_exposed_mutation_surface.update_file: repository_full_name + path + replacement content + current file blob sha + optional branch; no repository id/node id/expected repository incarnation/If-Match field is exposed.
current_exposed_mutation_surface.create_file_delete_file: repository_full_name + path (+ file blob sha for delete) + optional branch; no repository-incarnation compare is exposed.
current_exposed_mutation_surface.create_tree_create_commit: repository_full_name plus Git-object inputs; target repository is still selected by owner/name and no repository-incarnation precondition is exposed.
current_exposed_mutation_surface.update_ref_create_branch: repository_full_name + branch/ref name + commit sha; update_ref can require non-force fast-forward, but no expected old ref SHA or repository-id compare is exposed by the connector.
current_exposed_mutation_surface.capability_narrowing: No current Chat-exposed GitHub mutation action found in this bounded audit can atomically bind both logical repository owner/name and immutable repository incarnation to the same write.

public_source_basis.observation: Create/update file contents addresses the repository by owner and repo; update requires the blob SHA of the file being replaced and optionally a branch name. The documented mutation parameter set contains no repository id/node id precondition.

Update a reference addresses owner/repo/ref and supplies the new SHA plus optional force; force=false constrains fast-forward but the documented parameters contain no repository-incarnation compare and no expected-old-ref parameter.
Repository reads expose repository metadata including stable numeric id/node_id, but the tested write endpoints are still owner/name addressed rather than id-preconditioned.
GitHub documents ETag conditional requests as conditional GET optimization; this does not supply the missing write-time repository-incarnation fence for the tested mutation actions.

repo_id_precheck_then_contents_blob_sha_.unsafe_condition: repository rebind occurs after the metadata precheck and the replacement contains the same expected file blob; stale update can satisfy the file-SHA CAS in the replacement repository because repository identity is not part of the atomic mutation precondition.
repo_id_precheck_then_contents_blob_sha_.safe_fail_closed: 4/16 rebind traces where replacement does not contain the required blob/history; remaining 8/16 have no rebind.

contents_branch_plus_blob_sha_write.unsafe_condition: same branch name and same expected blob exist in the replacement; branch name plus content-addressed blob SHA identifies state, not repository incarnation.

immutable_git_objects_then_named_ref_pub.unsafe_condition: replacement imports/recreates the same required Git history/object identities, so a later owner/name-addressed publication can target the replacement. Immutable object identity does not by itself bind the destination repository incarnation.

fast_forward_named_ref_update.unsafe_condition: replacement contains a compatible identical/imported history; fast-forward validity is evaluated inside whichever repository owner/name resolves at mutation time and therefore does not prove old repository incarnation.

aggregate.duplicate_effect_from_response_loss: 0 additional repository-local duplicates in this model when Part127 stable semantic edge/effect identity is retained; the defect is wrong-incarnation mutation, not replay classification.
aggregate.rate_limit_or_lost_response_behavior: Checkpoint and defer exact readback to the next scheduled invocation; no lease expiry, same-run poll, or finite-credit rescue is introduced. Deferral does not repair a mutation that already landed in the wrong repository incarnation.

finding.new_narrowing: Part127's file/blob CAS plus stable semantic generation-edge identity remains safe only after destination repository incarnation is fixed. A pre-read repository id is TOCTOU evidence, not a write fence. Branch/ref names and Git object SHAs can also survive or be recreated by import/restore, so they cannot generically distinguish old and same-name replacement repositories. The current Chat-exposed GitHub write actions audited here expose no atomic repository-id/incarnation compare.
finding.exact_missing_capability: A Chat-exposed zero-cost mutation primitive whose success predicate atomically includes both the current logical state CAS (file/blob/ref/generation) and an immutable destination repository-incarnation identifier, or an equivalent server-enforced destination capability that cannot be valid after same-name delete/recreate/rebind.

unresolved_children.detail: Precheck-only repository identity is not atomic with the later owner/name-addressed write.
Test sink-side stable effect identity + generation/claim-owner fencing for non-repository useful effects without hosted coordination, finite quota, or richer-mode arbitration.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.richer_mode_protected_manual_execution_d: none for the bounded repository transport audit/model itself; the missing repository-incarnation fence remains unresolved rather than handed off
zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.quota_zero_scope_guard: The candidate transport uses lightweight repository APIs only and tolerates rate-limit interruption through cross-invocation checkpoint/resume. This is not a claim of continuous API availability or paid-plan independence.

continuation: Part129: execute one bounded external-effect generation/effect-fencing leaf. Keep Part127 replay semantics and Part128 repository-incarnation blocker explicit. Model a non-repository sink with stable effect_id, generation/claim-owner fence, response loss, duplicate delivery, sink reset/rebind, rate-limit interruption, and later retry. Compare sink-local monotonic fence, request-id-only dedupe with expiry, repository precheck plus unfenced sink write, and fail-closed sink capability tokens. Require zero external hosted coordination, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency, zero incremental cost, and no richer-mode/protected/manual execution handoff.
